title: Stickman Adblocker
description: This is a fun project where I made an adblocker that has a stickman appear to remove your ads. It passes all tests on CanYouBlockIt.com, and has an interactive stickman that you can throw around.

title: Evac Assist
description: EvacAssist is an app that helps people in crisis areas find other users who have access to vehicles, allowing them to coordinate an evacuation. It shows a path from driver to passenger that avoids conflict zones in the region, has options for disabilities needed, number of passengers, and a live map. On the admin side, there is a web dashboard which allows for a quick overview of all users and current trips made.

title: Squat Counter
description: AI-powered squat counter using pretrained TensorFlow models. Won Best Use of AI/ML Award at Purdue Indy Hackathon 2025. Adapted TensorFlow models to fit project goals, planned and executed a weeklong project plan, continuing previous work on AI in sports and health.

title: Calorie Tracker Quick Project
description: Client database server website designed to help track calorie intake throughout the day. Built using SQL for backend and React for frontend.

title: Undergraduate Student Research
description: Analyzed sales, service, and replacement data to identify defect-prone products. Processed and organized 200,000+ data points to develop a predictive function for cumulative defects over six years. Identified six high-loss products through team analysis with $50,000+ impact.

title: Undergraduate Student Research - AI Healthcare Platform
description: Developing an AI-powered platform that provides real-time, patient-specific cost-saving recommendations. This innovative solution aims to reduce administrative burden, promote pharmacoequity, and improve health outcomes by making medication access easier for patients and providers. Research conducted under Dr. Alan Zillich - Pharm.D., FCCP.

title: Undergraduate Research Paper
description: Published research paper on an interactive algorithm utilizing a pose detection neural network to help martial arts students improve their forms during solo practice. Featured in Journal of Student Research with almost 400 downloads and 16+ references.

title: ToolBot
description: A 5-degree-of-freedom robotic arm that can identify and sort tools on its own. ToolBot was entirely 3D-printed, with custom gearing to keep it fast and reliable, and a modified YOLO algorithm trained on common workshop tools to handle object recognition in real time. Built as a hackathon project completed in a day and a half with excellent team coordination.
